It also replaces the convoluted, ambiguous modal construction with a plain past-tense statement of what was done. Version B splits the original run-on into cleaner sentences, but it keeps 'would have been expected to have been applied.' That phrase is grammatically tortured and reads as hedging in a methods section. B also leaves the sample size dangling at the end, detached from the exclusions that produce it. A places N right after the exclusion rule. On length, A spends words on the enumeration ('First... Second...'), while B spends them on the stacked modal. The two are roughly equally economical. Overall A is clearer, flows better, is more precise, and better suits a methods audience.
